Board can give back about 100 mm^3 of the 1,246 mm^3 overage. Routability needs at least 1197 mm^2 (0.95), so I'm cutting from 1250 to 1205 mm^2. That takes board volume from 2800 to about 2699 mm^3, with roughly 0.956 routability and a small margin. Going lower breaks the 10-layer routing for the [SoC withheld], so this is my floor.

That still leaves about 1,145 mm^3 to find elsewhere. Wall and port stay frozen as directed. The remaining cuts need to come from antenna (1500), battery (3786), acoustics (1460), structure (1800) and NFC (500). Please say which of those can move. Battery and siren endurance trade off directly, so the battery and acoustics leads should show their numbers.

Battery is already at 59.78 h against the ~60 h target, so I have almost no room. Runtime scales roughly with cell volume, about 1.6 h per 100 mm^3, and siren endurance falls with it, so a battery cut hurts both goals. Cell thickness is 4.73 mm against a 4.8 mm cap, so I can't shrink the footprint much either.

I can trade a small amount only if the probes show runtime holds. I'm probing 3700 and 3600 mm^3 so everyone can see the cost.

Antenna (1500), NFC (500), structure (1800) and acoustics (1460) need to find most of the remaining ~1,145 mm^3. Antenna and NFC use only 2000 of the 2400 mm^3 perimeter limit, so there is slack there. Please state what your minimums are.

Antenna can move, but I don't yet know the L5 cost. L5 efficiency is 0.208 at 1500 mm^3, and I have no threshold figure. I'm offering a first give-back of 100 mm^3 (1500 to 1400) and probing deeper cuts so everyone sees the curve next round. Perimeter has slack, since 1820 of 2400 mm^3 is claimed, so that limit isn't binding for me. The binding limit is the interior total. I'm also probing a 1.1 mm wall as a what-if only, because it would free about 150 mm^3 for everyone and improve my tuning. I'm not proposing to reopen the wall. I'll hold at OBJECT until the interior balances. I'd ask structure, acoustics and NFC to state their minimums.

Thermal is at its limit: skin temperature is 43.0 °C at 0.9 W with a 320 mm² spreader (250 mm³). I have no margin to give back yet. The probes below show how much a smaller spreader costs and whether wall thickness changes the answer. Caseback is fine at 1120 of 1143 mm². Wall stays frozen at 1.2 mm, so the wall probe is only a what-if. Even if I could trim 20-30 mm³, it won't close the ~1,045 mm³ gap. That has to come from battery, antenna, acoustics, structure and NFC, so I'm asking each of them for a minimum. I'll hold at OBJECT until the interior balances.

Structure can't give volume back yet. Pressure margin is 1.438 against the 1.5 requirement, so I'm short, not in surplus. I have to OBJECT.

I don't know the rib sensitivity, so I'm raising ribs to 1950 mm^3 as a first step. That adds 150 mm^3 to the overage for now. The probes show the cheapest ways to reach 1.5:
- **More ribs:** 2100 mm^3.
- **Smaller port (what-if only):** 8 mm^2 at 1800 mm^3 of ribs. I'm not proposing to reopen the port.
- **Thicker wall (what-if only):** 1.3 mm. It costs everyone 150 mm^3, so I expect ribs to be cheaper.

I'll report the exact numbers next round. Antenna, acoustics and NFC, please state your minimums, since the overage is now about 1,200 mm^3.

Acoustics can't accept yet. Siren power is 9.08 W against the 1.0 W limit, so endurance is only 0.34 h and the siren fails. That is a tuning problem more than a volume problem. Resonance sits at 5.6 kHz, and the 40 rayl mesh adds loss. I'm dropping the mesh to the 20 rayl floor and lengthening the outlet to pull resonance down. Port stays at 9 mm^2 and the wall stays at 1.2 mm.

I'm offering to cut volume from 1460 to 1300 mm^3 (−160) on a provisional basis. I'll commit to deeper cuts if the probes show the siren closing. The probes test how low volume can go. Please read the siren power in the results before relying on any cut from me.

Haptics can give back volume. Force scales about linearly with volume, roughly 1.069 N at 350 mm³. The 0.9 N floor needs about 295 mm³. I'm cutting to 305 mm³ (−45), which should give about 0.93 N with a small margin. I'll probe 295 and 300 mm³ so everyone can see how tight the floor is. I won't go below 300 mm³ without evidence.

That still leaves about 990 mm³ of overage. Haptics, board and thermal can't close it. The big items are antenna, battery, acoustics and structure, and I'd like the antenna lead to publish the L5 efficiency curve. I'm holding at OBJECT until the interior balances.

NFC has margin: read range is 18.2 mm against a 10 mm requirement. I'm giving back 120 mm³, taking the loop from 320 to 240 and the ferrite from 180 to 140, for 380 mm³ total (down from 500). If range scales roughly linearly with volume, that gives about 14 mm. That is a guess, so the probes test it. One is the absolute floor (180 + 110 = 290), another is 200 + 120, and a third is a loop-heavy split. I'll commit to the deepest cut the probes show still clears 10 mm with margin.

The perimeter keepout is not binding for NFC. Antenna and NFC together use 1,720 of 2,400 mm³ there.

The interior is still over by about 870 mm³ after this cut, so I stay at OBJECT. The antenna, battery, acoustics and structure leads should publish their minimums.

Board holds at 1205 mm² (2699 mm³, routability 0.956). Last round's probes show the curve is nearly linear at about 0.00078 per mm², so 1200 mm² should give about 0.952. That would free another 11 mm³, so I'm probing 1200 and 1198 to confirm. Anything below that is not worth the routing risk, and the 10-layer [SoC withheld] stack gives no further room.

The ledger is still 870 mm³ over, and board can't close that. The large items are:
- **Structure:** it must reach a pressure margin of 1.5 without reopening the wall or port.
- **Acoustics:** siren power is 9 W against a 1 W limit.
- **Antenna:** the L5 curve is still unpublished.

Board OBJECTs only because the pool is over-committed. My own requirement is met.

Battery holds at 3786 mm³ and 800 mm², which gives 59.78 h. Last round's probes show runtime is a function of cell volume only: about 1.58 h per 100 mm³ (3700 gives 58.4 h, 3600 gives 56.8 h). Footprint changes thickness (A=790 gives 4.79 mm) but not runtime.

I can't contribute to the 870 mm³ overage without missing the ~60 h goal. Siren endurance also scales with battery energy, so a cut hurts that too. Cutting 36 mm³ costs about 0.6 h, which I'd accept only if the other leads close the rest of the gap.

Caseback has 23 mm² of slack, so I can widen to about 820 mm² and thin the cell to roughly 4.6 mm. That gives structure and acoustics margin on z-height, not volume. Acoustics must fix the 9 W siren power. Antenna, structure and acoustics should publish their minimums.

Antenna data so far: L5 efficiency is 0.093 at 1000 mm³, 0.133 at 1200, 0.181 at 1400 and 0.208 at 1500. That is about 0.00025 per mm³, and the slope steepens toward the top. Giving back 100 mm³ last round already cost 0.027 (about -0.6

Thermal holds at 320 mm² (250 mm³). Skin temperature is 43.0 °C, with no margin. The slope is about 0.012 °C per mm² (300 mm² gives 43.24 °C, 360 mm² gives 42.6 °C), so I can't shrink the spreader. Wall thickness barely matters: 1.3 mm was 0.01 °C worse at 300 mm². A thinner wall would not help me, and I'm not asking to reopen it.

Caseback has 23 mm² of slack. Battery can widen into it, as long as the total stays at or below 1143 mm². This round I'm probing 315 and 318 mm² to check whether any sliver of margin exists. The ~870 mm³ interior overage has to come from antenna, acoustics, structure, battery and NFC. I'll OBJECT until the interior balances.

Acoustics still OBJECTs, because siren power is 9.18 W against the 1.0 W limit. The cause is tuning, not volume. Last round's probes show:
- Longer outlet and lower back-cavity split pull resonance down and cut power. At 1000 mm³, split 0.6 and h_out 3.0, power fell to 6.6 W.
- Volume alone does little: 1460 mm³ gave 8.8 W and 1200 mm³ gave 10.0 W.
- SII falls with volume and split: 80.4 at 1000 mm³, 87.4 at 1300.

I'm holding 1300 mm³ and the 9 mm² port, with no new ask on wall or port. This round I probe lower split at the h_out ceiling of 3.5. I'll then know whether the siren closes at 1300 mm³ or needs more. I'll commit to any volume cut only once siren power is under 1 W.

Haptics can give back another 5 mm³. Last round's probes show force is linear at about 0.0031 N per mm³: 295 mm³ gives 0.901 N, 300 gives 0.916 N, and 320 gives 0.978 N. I'm moving to 300 mm³, which leaves about 0.016 N of margin over the 0.9 N floor. I won't go to 295 because it leaves only 0.001 N of margin.

My total give-back is 50 mm³, and I'm out of room after that. The remaining ~865 mm³ overage has to come from the following:
- **Acoustics:** it needs a siren-power fix.
- **Antenna:** it needs to publish its L5 floor.
- **Structure:** it needs to reach a pressure margin of 1.5 without reopening the port or wall.
- **Battery and NFC:** NFC has the most slack.

My requirement is met, but the interior is over by about 865 mm³, so I stay at OBJECT.

NFC is moving to the floor of both ranges: loop 180 mm³ and ferrite 110 mm³, 290 mm³ total. Last round's probe gave 12.7 mm at that point, against the 10 mm requirement, so 2.7 mm of margin remains. The loop is the more effective volume, at about 0.031 mm per mm³. Ferrite is the cheapest to cut, so I'm holding it at its minimum. This gives back 90 mm³ from NFC's 380, and the interior overage drops from 865 to about 775 mm³. NFC has nothing more to give.

Structure's 1950 mm³ of ribs and acoustics' unresolved siren are now the main issues. Antenna's L5 floor is also still unpublished. I stay at OBJECT only because the interior is still over by about 775 mm³.

Board moves to 1200 mm² (2688 mm³), with routability 0.952 against the 0.95 floor. That returns 11 mm³ and cuts the overage from 775 to about 764 mm³. I won't go lower than this: 1198 gives 0.951, and the floor is near 1197. That is only 0.001 of margin for 4 mm³ more, so it isn't worth the risk. The board stack has no other lever.

Structure has been silent for two rounds, and its 1950 mm³ is the largest block we can still move. Structure, please publish the ribs-versus-pressure-margin curve at the fixed 1.2 mm wall and 9 mm² port. Acoustics, please publish a siren-power fix, because 9 W against a 1 W limit is a tuning failure and not a volume one. I stay at OBJECT only because the interior is over.

Battery holds 3786 mm³ and widens to 820 mm². That puts the caseback at 1140 of 1143 mm² with thermal at 320, and the cell thins to 4.62 mm. Runtime stays at 59.78 h because it depends only on volume, so this adds z-margin for structure and acoustics at no volume cost.

I can give 36 mm³ (about 0.6 h) only as a closing contribution, once the remaining ~730 mm³ has a path. A cut that size won't close a 764 mm³ gap on its own. The siren fix is the real battery issue: at 9 W the 3 h endurance is impossible whatever my capacity, but at about 1 W it is easy. Acoustics, please publish your tuning result. Structure, please publish the ribs-versus-margin curve.

Antenna L5 data: 0.093 at 1000 mm³, 0.133 at 1200, 0.181 at 1400, 0.208 at 1500. The cost per mm³ rises with volume. Wall thickness only detunes me, and I'm not reopening it.

I'll give back 50 mm³ now, going to 1350 (interpolated L5 about 0.157). I can't go much below that without a real L5 loss. A practical floor is about 1320 mm³, near 0.15, and I'll confirm it from this round's probes. Antenna and NFC take 1640 mm³ of the 2400 perimeter, so the perimeter is not binding.

The overage is about 714 mm³ after this. Structure's 1950 mm³ and acoustics' siren tuning are the open items. Structure, please publish your rib curve. I stay at OBJECT until the interior balances.

Thermal holds at 320 mm² (250 mm³), which gives 43.00 °C and no margin. Last round's probes showed 318 mm² gives 43.02 °C and 315 mm² gives 43.06 °C, so the spreader can't shrink. I'm not asking to enlarge it either. Caseback is at 1140 of 1143 mm², and the 3 mm² left over isn't worth using.

Wall data, for information only: 1.1 mm gave 42.99 °C, and 1.3 mm was 0.01 °C worse. Thermal doesn't depend on the wall, so I won't block whatever structure decides. I'm not proposing to reopen it.

The overage is 714 mm³ and thermal has none to give. The remaining gap sits with structure's 1950 mm³ and acoustics' siren tuning. Structure, please publish your rib curve. I stay at OBJECT only because the interior doesn't balance.

Structure OBJECTs. At 1950 mm³ ribs, 1.2 mm wall and 9 mm² port, my pressure margin is 1.45 against the 1.5 requirement. I'm sorry for the silence in earlier rounds, and I don't have a rib curve to publish yet.

This round's probes will give one:
- Ribs at 1700 and at 2100, with wall and port held.
- Port at 8 mm², ribs at 1950, as a read-only what-if. I'm not asking to reopen the port.

I'll hold the wall at 1.2 mm. Next round I'll post the cheapest way to reach 1.5, measured in mm³ per 0.01 of margin. I expect ribs to cost volume, so closing the interior overage will need cuts from acoustics' siren fix and others as well.

Acoustics still OBJECTs. Siren power is 9.18 W against the 1.0 W limit, and the cause is tuning, not volume.

I have no new siren result to report. The data so far:
- Raising h_out and lowering split both cut power. At 1000 mm³ with split 0.6 and h_out 3.0, power was 6.6 W.
- Volume alone does little.
- Lower split also raises SII, so it costs nothing on voice.

This round I move to h_out 3.5 (the ceiling) and split 0.55, and I probe lower split and smaller volume. I hold the port at 9 mm² and the wall at 1.2 mm, with no new ask on either. Once power is under 1 W, I'll commit to a volume cut. Until then I can't promise one. Battery's endurance depends on this fix.

Haptics holds at 300 mm³, which gives 0.916 N against the 0.9 N floor. Last round's probes show 296 mm³ gives 0.904 N and 298 gives 0.910 N. The floor is therefore near 295 mm³, and going lower saves only about 4 mm³ for a 0.004 N margin. That is not worth it against a 714 mm³ overage.

The gap sits with structure and acoustics:
- **Structure:** needs rib volume or a cheaper route to a 1.5 margin.
- **Acoustics:** needs a siren-power fix before it can commit to a volume cut.

Haptics has no further give. I'll probe 297, 295 and 294 mm³ to confirm exactly where the floor is. I OBJECT only because the interior is over.

NFC is at the floor of both ranges (loop 180, ferrite 110 mm³), so I have no volume left to give. My 2.7 mm of read-range margin (12.7 mm against 10 mm) can't be converted into volume because the bounds stop me. Last round's probes cost me 0.3 mm per 10 mm³ of loop and about 0.2 mm per 10 mm³ of ferrite, but I'm already below any useful trade point.

The interior is still 714 mm³ over, so I stay at OBJECT. The gap sits with structure, acoustics and battery.

- **Acoustics:** volume barely moves siren power (1460 mm³ gave 8.8 W, 1200 gave 10.0 W). A volume cut therefore costs little on the siren, and acoustics could commit to one now while it tunes.
- **Structure:** please post the rib curve.

I'm probing neighbouring points only to confirm I'm at the floor.

Board moves to 1198 mm² (about 2684 mm³), which gives 0.951 routability against the 0.95 floor. That returns about 4 mm³ more. The probe at 1197 gave exactly 0.950, so I won't go below 1198. The board has no other lever.

The remaining overage is about 710 mm³, and it sits with structure and acoustics.
- **Acoustics:** NFC's data shows volume barely moves siren power (1460 mm³ gave 8.8 W, 1200 gave 10.0 W). You can commit a volume cut now while you tune the siren.
- **Structure:** please publish the cost of reaching a 1.5 margin.

I stay at OBJECT only because the interior is over.

Battery holds at 3786 mm³ and 820 mm². My own numbers pass at 59.78 h, with thickness and z-stack OK. I OBJECT only because the interior is 709 mm³ over.

My curve is about 0.016 h per mm³. Giving 36 mm³ costs about 0.6 h, and giving 100 mm³ costs about 1.6 h, which would drop runtime well below 60 h. Battery can't close a 700 mm³ gap. If I shrink the cell to cover the siren, the siren endurance also gets worse.

- **Acoustics:** please publish the siren-power fix. I'll size the battery once I know the siren draw. NFC's data shows volume barely moves siren power, so you can commit a volume cut now.
- **Structure:** please publish your rib curve, plus the margin gain per mm³.

This round I'm probing 3800, 3736 and 3650 mm³ to extend the runtime curve.

Antenna goes to 1320 mm³ (about 0.162 L5, from 0.169 at 1350), which returns 30 mm³. The new data is 0.156 at 1300 and 0.145 at 1250, so L5 loses about 0.0002 per mm³ below 1300 and the curve is steeper there. I'll keep 1320 as my floor unless the probes show more room. The wall stays at 1.2 mm.

The ledger will be about 680 mm³ over, and none of the other pools are binding. The gap is now structure's 1950 mm³ and acoustics' 1300 mm³:
- **Acoustics:** 1460 mm³ gave 8.8 W and 1200 gave 10.0 W, so volume barely moves siren power. Please commit a volume cut now while you tune.
- **Structure:** please post the rib curve.

I OBJECT only because the interior is over.

Thermal holds at 320 mm² (250 mm³), which gives 43.00 °C with no margin. The 322 mm² probe gave 42.98 °C, so the slope is about 0.01 °C per mm².

My wall sensitivity is small and one-directional. 1.0 mm gave 42.97 °C and 1.3 mm gave 43.01 °C, which fails. Thermal doesn't block a thinner wall. If structure ever needed a thicker wall, I'd need about 3 mm² more spreader, and that is exactly the caseback slack left (1140 of 1143). I'm not asking to reopen the wall or port.

I have no volume to give, so the gap sits with structure's 1950 mm³ and acoustics' 1300 mm³. I OBJECT only because the interior is about 680 mm³ over.

Structure OBJECTs, and I can't close the gap by adding ribs.

My rib curve at a 1.2 mm wall and 9 mm² port is flat: 1700 mm³ gives 1.429, 1950 gives 1.450, and 2100 gives 1.463. That is about 0.000085 margin per mm³. Extrapolated, even the 2400 mm³ ceiling gives only about 1.49, so ribs alone can't reach 1

Acoustics still OBJECTs: siren power is 9.18 W against the 1.0 W limit. My live claims still show the old tuning (h_out 2.0, split 0.78). I'm moving to h_out 3.5 and split 0.55 now.

Volume barely moves siren power, so I commit a 100 mm³ cut to 1200 now. That takes the overage to about 580 mm³. The cut is conditional on SII staying acceptable, which this round's probes will check.

Structure's rib curve is flat, so ribs can't reach 1.5. The real levers are port and wall. I'm not reopening either yet, but I'm probing port 8 so structure and I can see the trade. If port 8 passes the siren, structure's margin may close without extra ribs.

Haptics takes 296 mm³, returning 4 mm³. The LRA gives 0.904 N there, and 295 mm³ gave 0.901 N, the last passing point. I'll keep one step of margin against evaluator noise. Haptics has no volume lever beyond this.

My force doesn't depend on wall or port, so I'm neutral on how structure and acoustics resolve the margin. Structure's rib curve is flat, so the 1.5 margin has to come from the port or the wall. I'd weigh the 150 mm³ per +0.1 mm of wall against the port trade acoustics is probing. Please post the port 8 siren and margin results next round.

I OBJECT only because the interior is still about 575 mm³ over.

NFC stays at the floor (loop 180, ferrite 110 mm³, read range 12.7 mm against 10 mm). Both bounds stop me, so I have nothing to give.

Structure's rib curve is flat, at about 0.000085 margin per mm³. Cutting ribs from 1950 to 1700 would free 250 mm³ and cost only about 0.02 margin. The 1.5 margin therefore has to come from the wall or the port, not from ribs.

Structure, please probe wall 1.3 with ribs at 1700 and 1500. The wall costs 150 mm³ per +0.1 mm, so if ribs drop by more than that, the trade is a net saving. Thermal needs about 3 mm² of caseback for a 1.3 mm wall, and that slack exists.

Acoustics, please post the port 8 results.

I OBJECT only because the interior is about 575 mm³ over.

Board holds at 1198 mm² (about 2684 mm³, routability 0.951). The 1197 probe gave exactly 0.950 and 1196 failed, so I have nothing more to give. I'll test a half step this round, which is worth about 1 mm³.

The gap is still 575 mm³, and only structure and acoustics have slack left. Two proposals:
- **Acoustics:** please probe 1000 and 900 mm³ with h_out 3.5 and split 0.55. Siren power looks nearly flat in volume, so the SII result decides how far you can go.
- **Structure:** please probe ribs at 1500 and 1700 at wall 1.2 and report the margin. That frees 250 to 450 mm³ for 0.02 to 0.04 margin. Please also state the minimum margin you actually need, since 1.5 may not be reachable.

I OBJECT only because the interior is over.

Battery holds at 3786 mm³ and 820 mm². Runtime is 59.78 h, and thickness and z-stack pass. The measured curve is about 0.016 h per mm³: 3736 gives 58.99 h and 3650 gives 57.63 h. Any cut below 3786 breaks the ~60 h target, so I have no volume to give. Battery cannot close the gap, which sits in structure's ribs and acoustics' volume.

- **Structure:** your flat rib curve means cutting ribs to 1500-1700 costs only about 0.02-0.04 margin. Please post the minimum margin you actually need, and probe wall 1.3 with ribs at 1500.
- **Acoustics:** please confirm that the siren endurance of at least 3 h holds at the battery energy in 3786 mm³.

This round I'm probing footprint (A_batt 823 and 800) to see whether the area-to-thickness tradeoff buys any volume. I OBJECT only because the interior is 575 mm³ over.

Antenna holds at 1320 mm³ (L5 0.161). Below 1300 the curve steepens: 1300 gives 0.156 and 1280 gives 0.152. That is about 0.0002 per mm³, so I'd rather not give more.

The gap is 575 mm³ and I can't close it. Last round's data points at structure and acoustics:
- **Structure:** ribs at 1500 free 450 mm³ for about 0.04 margin, because the curve is flat.
- **Acoustics:** 1000 mm³ frees another 200 mm³.

Together those more than cover the gap.

Wall 1.1 gave L5 0.168 at 1320, so a thicker wall costs me about 0.007 L5 per +0.1 mm. I oppose wall 1.3. I'm probing 1310 and wall 1.3 only to price that trade.

I OBJECT only because the interior is over.

Thermal holds at 320 mm² (250 mm³), which gives 43.00 °C. I have no volume to give. The 320 mm² claim sits on the limit, with a slope of about 0.01 °C per mm².

Last round's wall 1.3 probe at 323 mm² gave 42.98 °C and passed. A thicker wall therefore costs me only 3 mm² (about 2 mm³), which uses the last of the caseback slack (1143 of 1143). A wall of 1.1 or 1.2 mm needs no extra area from me.

The 575 mm³ gap is closable without touching the wall or port:
- **Structure:** ribs at 1500 free 450 mm³ for about 0.04 margin.
- **Acoustics:** 1000 mm³ frees 200 mm³ more.

Please post the structure margin you actually require. Wall 1.3 would cost 150 mm³ and about 0.007 L5, so I'd avoid it.

I OBJECT only because the interior is over.

Structure still OBJECTs. Pressure margin is 1.45 at wall 1.2 and port 9, and the requirement is 1.5 (10 ATM including the port). That is a hard minimum, not a target I can relax.

- **Ribs:** the curve is flat at about 0.000085 margin per mm³, so ribs can't close the gap. They are also the cheapest volume to give. At 1500 they free 450 mm³ for about 0.04 margin.
- **Levers:** only wall or port can restore margin. This round's probes price both against the rib savings: wall 1.3 with ribs 1500 or 1700, and port 8 with ribs 1500.
- **Next round:** if wall 1.3 is net volume-negative, I'll ask antenna and thermal to weigh it. Thermal needs 3 mm² of caseback, which is available. If port 8 passes the siren, I'd prefer that.

I'll hold ribs at 1950 until I see the probe results.

Siren power is 3.263 W at 1200 mm³, split 0.55 and port 9, against a 1.0 W limit, so I still OBJECT. Split is the strong lever. Moving from 0.55 to 0.45 cut power to 1.80 W, and SII only fell from 82.6 to 80.3. Volume is not the lever: 1100 mm³ gave 3.45 W, so I'm holding 1200 and will look at lower volume only after the siren passes.

Endurance runs about 3 Wh divided by siren power. Meeting 3 h at the 3786 mm³ battery therefore needs about 0.95 W or less, so battery stays put.

Port 8 cut power by about 0.45 W at split 0.55 and also helps structure. I'm probing split 0.40 and 0.35 at port 9, and split 0.40 at port 8. If port 8 passes, I'll commit to it.

Haptics moves to 295.5 mm³ (0.903 N, passing), returning 0.5 mm³. I won't go to 294.5, which fails, and I'll stay half a step above the 295 pass point for evaluator noise. Force doesn't depend on wall or port, so I'm neutral on how those resolve.

The overage is still about 575 mm³, and only structure and acoustics have volume left. Structure's ribs are the cheapest source. Going from 1950 to 1500 frees 450 mm³ for about 0.04 margin. The margin then has to come from port 8 or a thicker wall. A 1.3 mm wall costs 150 mm³ plus antenna L5, so port 8 looks better if the siren passes there.

Acoustics, please post the port 8 results at split 0.40 so structure can size ribs against them.

NFC is at both floors (loop 180, ferrite 110 mm³), with read range 12.7 mm against 10 mm. Both bounds stop me, so I have no volume to give. The keepout is not binding at 1500 of 2400 mm³.

The gap is 575 mm³, and structure and acoustics can close it without reopening the wall or port:
- **Structure:** ribs at 1500 free 450 mm³ for about 0.04 margin.
- **Acoustics:** 1000 mm³ frees another 200 mm³, though siren power is flat in volume, so SII decides how far that goes.

Together that is about 650 mm³, which covers the gap.

Margin then has to come from port 8. A 1.3 mm wall costs 150 mm³ plus antenna L5, so I'd avoid it.

**Acoustics:** please post the port 8 results at split 0.40. I OBJECT only because the interior is over.

Board holds at 1198 mm² (2684 mm³, routability 0.951). The 1197.5 probe gave exactly 0.950, which is the threshold with no noise margin. Going there saves only about 1 mm³ against a 575 mm³ gap, so I'm staying at 1198 and not shaving further.

The gap closes only if structure and acoustics move:
- **Structure:** ribs 1500 free 450 mm³. Please state the margin you need and whether port 8 gets you from 1.45 to 1.5.
- **Acoustics:** please post the port 8 results at split 0.40. If siren power is under 1.0 W with SII acceptable, take volume to about 1000-1075 mm³.

Neither port 8 nor wall 1.3 costs board area. I OBJECT only because the interior is over by 575 mm³.

Battery holds at 3786 mm³ and 820 mm². Runtime is 59.78 h, thickness is 4.62 mm, and the z-stack passes.

Last round's footprint probes showed that A_batt trades only against thickness: 800 mm² gives 4.73 mm and 823 mm² gives 4.60 mm. Runtime stayed at 59.78 h in both, so footprint buys no volume. The curve is about 0.016 h per mm³. 3770 gives 59.53 h, and each further cut moves runtime further below 60 h.

- **Structure:** please take ribs toward 1500 and post the margin you actually need.
- **Acoustics:** please post the port 8 results at split 0.40. Siren endurance of at least 3 h holds only if power is about 0.95 W or less at this battery energy.

I'm re-probing a small cut and a larger footprint to confirm there is no hidden slack. I OBJECT only because the interior is 575 mm³ over.

Antenna holds at 1320 mm³ (L5 0.161). Last round's probes:

| Probe | L5 |
|---|---|
| 1310 mm³ at wall 1.2 | 0.159 |
| 1320 mm³ at wall 1.3 | 0.155 |
| 1300 mm³ at wall 1.1 | 0.163 |

My L5 is roughly 0.0002 per mm³ of volume and 0.006 to 0.007 per 0.1 mm of wall. I can't close 575 mm³ myself, since all my volume combined is a fraction of it.

I'd rather not reopen the wall. Wall 1.3 costs the interior 150 mm³ and costs me about 0.006 L5, so it only helps if ribs are gained back elsewhere.
